headline: Growth hormone
body: The same total amount does different things depending on how it arrives.
punch: Pattern beats quantity, and that was shown in 1988.

headline: Every discussion
body: How many units. How much your body makes. Whether that number is high or low. The entire conversation is a quantity argument.
punch: Your body never delivers it as a quantity. It delivers it as a rhythm.

headline: The experiment
body: Hypophysectomised rats — no endogenous growth hormone at all. Then GH was infused either in pulses or continuously, and skeletal tissue was measured.
punch: Same hormone, same animal, different delivery pattern.

headline: Pulsatile won
body: Pulsatile infusion more effectively increased IGF-1 messenger RNA specifically in skeletal tissue than continuous infusion did.
punch: The tissue responded to the pattern, not just the presence.

headline: Which means
body: Two protocols delivering identical total hormone can produce different skeletal responses. Dose alone doesn't determine the outcome — timing is part of the signal.

headline: Your own secretion
body: Natural GH release comes in bursts, largest during deep sleep, with low troughs between. That trough is not wasted time — it's part of the signal structure.

headline: Which is why
body: Arguments about whether an administered amount matches natural production compare a total to a rhythm. Those aren't the same kind of quantity.
punch: You can match the total and miss the signal entirely.

headline: The honest limits
body: Hypophysectomised rats, IGF-1 mRNA as the endpoint, not final height. It establishes that pattern matters mechanistically — not by how much in humans.
punch: Pattern matters. Magnitude in humans unmeasured.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
